meta.title: TabHero — Another tab? It’s already open.
meta.description: New chat. Same tab. TabHero opens chat links inside the WhatsApp Web page you already have loaded, preserving your session.
meta.ogTitle: TabHero. Another tab? It’s already open.
meta.ogDescription: New chat. Same tab. A small open-source extension for one less unnecessary detour.

strings.hero_p_006: NOT ALL HEROES OPEN NEW TABS.

You wanted to start a chat.

strings.hero_p_010: __BRAND__ takes the link to the WhatsApp Web page you already have loaded and opens the chat right there. The number and text come along. Your session stays put.

strings.perguntas_summary_119: Is this an official WhatsApp extension?+
strings.perguntas_p_120: No. __BRAND__ is an independent project, with no affiliation, sponsorship, or endorsement from WhatsApp or Meta. WhatsApp is a trademark of its respective owners.
strings.perguntas_p_122: The core goal is to open the chat inside the document that’s already loaded. __BRAND__ uses internal app commands. If the integration fails, it shows an error; it doesn’t reload the tab as a fallback.
strings.perguntas_p_124: Quick reply reads names, unread counts and the latest incoming text already loaded in WhatsApp. It sends only when you click Send. Saved replies and your OpenRouter key stay in this browser profile; drafts last for the browser session. On Suggest, the displayed received text and your draft go to OpenRouter and its AI provider. There is no telemetry or chat archive.
strings.perguntas_p_126: It’s still experimental. Automated tests run in Chromium and Firefox with a simulated WhatsApp interface. They check that the document, state, and draft are preserved, but don’t prove the integration works in a real signed-in session. WhatsApp’s internal modules can change.
strings.perguntas_p_128: The tab must be in the same browser and profile as the extension. Links without a number, groups, and channels follow their normal flow. If WhatsApp isn’t open, an initial tab is created. Temporary Firefox installations need to be repeated after restarting the browser.
strings.perguntas_summary_129: What if this becomes a built-in feature?+
strings.perguntas_p_130: We’ll happily retire the extension. What matters is getting the chat to the right place. The idea is here. So is the code.
strings.open_invitation_p_131: SMALL IDEAS DESERVE TO BECOME THE DEFAULT.
strings.open_invitation_h2_132:
The best version of __BRAND__?
The one nobody needs to install.
strings.open_invitation_p_133: Until then, the code is open. To test, improve, and keep the conversation moving.

privacy.title: Privacy — TabHero
privacy.heading:
Your chats.
The details, clear.
privacy.extensionP1: TabHero opens numbered chat links in an already loaded WhatsApp Web tab. Its optional quick-reply panel reads loaded chat names, unread counts and the latest incoming text so you can select a recipient, write or reuse a reply, and explicitly send through that session without focusing or reloading WhatsApp. It does not fetch a message archive or automatically send replies.
privacy.extensionP2: Saved replies and your optional OpenRouter key are stored locally in this browser profile, without browser sync. Drafts and send-operation records use browser-session storage. The key is not injected into WhatsApp. Only clicking Suggest sends the displayed received text and your draft directly to OpenRouter and its AI provider, under their policies. There is no developer-operated relay, analytics, advertising or telemetry. The silent icon badge shows unread counts, with no message body or desktop notification.
privacy.siteP1: The files and fonts are hosted with the site. Our code creates no cookies, includes no trackers and asks for no chats, phone numbers or account. Your language choice stays in the page URL; we do not store it in a profile. The interactive illustration runs locally and does not connect to WhatsApp.
privacy.siteP2: GitHub Pages hosts this website. As the hosting provider, GitHub may process technical access information, such as IP addresses and network requests, under its privacy statement. This is separate from the extension.
privacy.fundingP: When the receiving profile is active, the support button takes you to GitHub Sponsors. You choose and confirm the amount, frequency and payment there. This site receives no card details and does not confirm payments. While the profile is unavailable, the payment action stays disabled.
privacy.reportP: Open an issue with versions and the behavior you observed. Do not include real phone numbers, messages, QR codes, cookies or credentials. For security reports, see SECURITY.md.
privacy.maintainerP: Maintained by Klederson Bueno. Independent project. Not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by WhatsApp or Meta.

community.title: Community notes — TabHero
community.description: Eight historical reports, the complaints behind them and the product insights we draw from them. Sources and limits included.
community.heading:
Real complaints.
Useful lessons.
community.lede: Eight public reports from 2020–2025. These are editorial summaries, not quotes, customer testimonials or proof of current behavior.
community.methods: Read the full curation and methodology
community.limits: These authors did not review TabHero. This is a small historical collection, not a prevalence study. Our interpretations are product decisions, not quotations. Real authenticated compatibility remains unverified.
community.topHeading: The right context beats the right tab count.
community.topBody: A chat belongs in the account and browser context the person chose. Preserving the loaded document is our engineering criterion; the reports do not prove that behavior.
community.brandNote: Tab. Here. Hero. A small rescue from an unnecessary detour.

reports.title: Already open. Opened again.
reports.summary: The Web option starts another instance despite an existing tab.
reports.insight: Preserve the loaded context; focusing a tab alone is not enough.
reports.context: Historical report. Rechecked in the parent discussion; no document-identity measurement.

reports.title: Right conversation. Wrong account.
reports.summary: A business Web flow prompts the app associated with a personal account.
reports.insight: Make browser and profile boundaries explicit. The destination must respect the person’s account choice.
reports.context: Separate personal and business accounts; not a test of arbitrary multi-account selection.

reports.title: Two profiles. One pushy desktop app.
reports.summary: Desktop routing disrupts unsaved-contact links previously used with separate browser profiles.
reports.insight: Keep occasional contact initiation simple without forcing address-book changes.
reports.context: Desktop Web profiles. No claim of cross-profile access or lost drafts.

reports.title: Customer work, meet another loading screen.
reports.summary: A team reports another Web instance and a loading wait from its dashboard.
reports.insight: Demonstrate continuity in a real workflow. Do not invent time-saving statistics.
reports.context: The author later said an earlier redirection problem appeared fixed in June 2020.

reports.title: Find the tab that is already there.
reports.summary: A user asks to activate an existing Web tab before creating another.
reports.insight: Reuse and document preservation are different acceptance criteria.
reports.context: Tridactyl customization. Proposed URL updates do not prove state preservation.

reports.title: A closed issue is not the whole answer.
reports.summary: A library ignores an active tab; a later commenter asks where the fix is.
reports.insight: Link the fix, affected version and verification steps when resolving a report.
reports.context: Third-party automation; closed as a duplicate, not a TabHero test.

reports.title: Open with… what, exactly?
reports.summary: Firefox on Ubuntu reaches an app chooser without a working handler.
reports.insight: Make the destination predictable and errors understandable.
reports.context: No existing Web tab is stated. This is routing uncertainty, not proof of duplicate tabs.

reports.title: The goal was a chat, not another installation.
reports.summary: Firefox Android suggests installation; the author later reports a working link variant.
reports.insight: Diagnose the person’s task and environment before recommending setup changes.
reports.context: Mobile case marked solved. It does not demonstrate a desktop Web defect.
